title: Incremental schema repair, guided fallbacks, and tool-call observability — acceptance criteria
creator: Priya Nair
description: Problem: as we roll out streaming structured outputs with function/tool callbacks, customers see unrecoverable failures when emitted fragments diverge from an expected schema or when downstream tools transiently fail. This ticket defines acceptance criteria for a combined mitigation strategy: 1) a lightweight incremental-schema repair mechanism (server-side repair suggestions and optional auto-rewrite), 2) explicit fallback hints for callers when tool invocation fails under partial emission, and 3) instrumented observability so failures are actionable. Scope covers API behavior, server-side heuristics, contract tests, and telemetry definitions. Out of scope: building a general-purpose schema migration language and client SDK upgrades beyond minimal backwards-compatible guidance.
acceptance_criteria: Schema negotiation: Server accepts schema version header (X-Emit-Schema-V) and responds with X-Emit-Schema-Ack indicating accepted version or chosen compatibility mode within 100ms for streaming and non-streaming endpoints.

Partial-object checkpoints: When an emission contains partial object fragments, the runtime must emit checkpoint markers (type: "checkpoint") every N seconds (configurable, default 3s) and at message boundaries so clients can resume from last checkpoint without reprocessing earlier fragments.

Repair hints: For fragments that fail strict validation, the server must emit a repair-hint frame that contains: path to failing field, expected type/schema snippet, and one suggested minimal correction. Repair-hint frames count as streamed structured frames and must not break streaming boundaries.

Soft-auto-rewrite toggle: Admins can enable 'soft-auto-rewrite' at the route level. When enabled and the repair-hint is unambiguous (single-field scalar type mismatch), the runtime may auto-rewrite the fragment and annotate the stream with a "rewritten" flag. All rewrites must be logged and surfaced in telemetry.

Tool-call graceful degradation: If a tool invocation fails transiently during a streaming session, runtime must: a) emit a tool-failure frame with retryable=true/false; b) include a 'fallback-suggestion' (e.g., alternate model, simplified payload) in the frame; c) attempt configured retries according to route policy. Clients must be able to opt into automatic tool fallback via a per-request flag.

Deterministic parse-reconciliation: For end-to-end tests, two separate consumers reading the same checkpointed stream (with same schema version) must reconcile to identical object state after applying replay log; any divergence is a failure.

Observability: For any repair-hint, auto-rewrite, or tool-failure event, runtime must emit telemetry with standardized labels: event_type, route, model, schema_version, user_id (if available), request_id, error_class, and latency_ms. Events must be queryable in Console within 10 minutes of occurrence.

Contract tests: Add automated contract tests that simulate schema drift, field-type flapping, tool transient failures, and high-throughput streaming; tests must pass in CI on both hosted and dedicated runtime images before release.
Backward compatibility: If client omits X-Emit-Schema-V, the runtime defaults to 'compat-mode:best-effort' and must not apply auto-rewrite unless explicitly enabled in route config.

Documentation & SDK guidance: Update PRD + docs with examples for using repair-hints and checkpoint-resume. Add a migration checklist for customers and one sample snippet for Node/Python showing how to resume from a checkpointed stream.
test_plan: Unit: validator accepts/rejects fragments and produces repair-hint payloads for 12 canonical mismatch cases (missing field, extra field, type mismatch, enum drift, nested object missing required child, array element type mismatch, truncated fragment).

Integration: end-to-end test harness spins up runtime + mock tool service; run 1k streaming messages with intermittent tool 503s and assert retry/fallback frames are emitted; assert no dropped final objects after resume from checkpoint.
Contract: run two-reader reconciliation test - start stream, capture checkpoints, simulate client restart and resume; assert identical state with golden fixture.
Load: 10k concurrent streaming sessions for 30 minutes with repair-hints injected at 2% of messages; ensure median latency impact <5% and P95 < 20% above baseline.
Security: confirm repair-hint metadata does not leak PII; run static audit against repair-hint fields.
qa_steps: Smoke: create sample route with soft-auto-rewrite enabled; feed intentionally malformed fragment; verify 'repair-hint' and 'rewritten' flag appear in stream and visible in Console traces.
Failure mode: flip soft-auto-rewrite off; repeat above; confirm repair-hint emitted but original fragment preserved and error code surfaced to client.
Tool failure: configure mock tool to return intermittent 503s; ensure tool-failure frames emitted, fallback-suggestion present, and configured retry policy respected.
Resume test: simulate client crash after checkpoint N; restart and resume with checkpoint token; verify objects after resume match pre-crash stream.
Telemetry: run queries in Console for events event_type in [repair-hint, auto-rewrite, tool-failure] filtered by route and verify fields described in acceptance criteria are present.
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (canary): Enable feature in internal staging and run full contract test suite. Monitor telemetry for unexpected spikes in repair-hint events.
Stage 2 (beta customers): Enable on 5 opt-in customer routes. Collect feedback, observe error rates and false-positive rewrites for 2 weeks.
Stage 3 (gradual): Roll out to 25% of traffic with auto-rewrite disabled by default; default to emitting repair-hint frames only.
Stage 4 (global): Enable auto-rewrite as opt-in route flag; flip default to 'enabled' only after meeting stability gates and customer opt-in metrics.
telemetry: metrics/event_count{event_type} - counter by repair-hint, auto-rewrite, tool-failure
histogram/repair_hint_latency_ms - time from fragment arrival to repair-hint emission
gauge/active_checkpointed_streams - number of streams with active checkpoints
logs/sample_rewrite - structured log containing original_fragment, rewritten_fragment, request_id (stored for 30 days)
error_class taxonomy: validation_error | transient_tool | non_recoverable | schema_mismatch
notes: Design feedback from May: prefer minimal repair-hints to avoid confusing downstream parsers. We intentionally limit auto-rewrite to single-field scalar mismatches in v1.
Performance note: repair-hint generation must be bounded to O(k) where k is number of fields in fragment to avoid tail-latency regression.
Legal/security: any auto-rewrite that modifies user-provided content requires audit logging for compliance customers.
